grammar: n. & v. 位置；职位；安置
collocations: a position in a company; take a position; position the chair near the window
commonMistake: position 是名词“职位/位置”或动词“安置”；谈工作时可说 apply for a position，不能把它和 position oneself（使自己处于某位置）混为一谈。

example.english: Mina applied for a teaching position at the new school.
example.chinese: 米娜申请了这所新学校的教师职位。

application.prompt: After three interviews, Mina was offered a ___ at the school. A. possession B. position
application.solution: B。解析：position 在招聘语境中指“职位”；possession 表示“财物/拥有”，不符合被录用的意思。

collocations: deep sadness; a feeling of sadness; overcome sadness
commonMistake: sadness 是不可数名词，由 sad 加 -ness 构成；表达“感到悲伤”用 feel sad，不能说 feel sadness 作表语。

example.english: The song filled the room with a quiet sadness.
example.chinese: 这首歌让整个房间弥漫着淡淡的忧伤。

application.prompt: After the team lost the final, the players felt ___ but thanked their fans. A. sadly B. sad
application.solution: B。解析：felt 后接形容词 sad 表示“感到难过”；sadly 是副词，不能直接作 feel 的表语。

collocations: run out of milk; time is running out; run out of supplies
commonMistake: 物品作主语时用 run out；人用完某物时说 run out of sth。

example.english: We ran out of clean water before the rescue team arrived.
example.chinese: 救援队到达前，我们的干净饮用水就用完了。

application.prompt: The generator stopped because the camp had ___ fuel. A. run out of B. run out
application.solution: A。解析：句中 fuel 是“用完”的宾语，因此用 run out of；run out 后不直接接宾语。

collocations: give a lecture on history; attend a lecture; a lecture hall
commonMistake: lecture 通常指较正式的讲授；“听讲座”说 attend/listen to a lecture，不说 hear a lecture 表示参加活动。

example.english: We attended a lecture about protecting sea turtles.
example.chinese: 我们听了一场关于保护海龟的讲座。

application.prompt: Dr Lee will ___ a lecture on online safety this Friday. A. give B. attend
application.solution: A。解析：give a lecture 表示“作讲座”；attend a lecture 是听众参加讲座。

collocations: react to the news; react quickly; reaction to a change
commonMistake: react 后常接介词 to；名词形式为 reaction。

example.english: The audience reacted warmly to the young pianist.
example.chinese: 观众热情地回应了这位年轻钢琴家的演奏。

application.prompt: How did the dog ___ when it heard the doorbell? A. react B. reaction
application.solution: A。解析：did 后用动词原形 react；reaction 是名词，不能放在助动词 did 后作谓语。

collocations: mix up the dates; mix A up with B; get the names mixed up
commonMistake: mix up A and B 表示把两者弄混；说“把 A 误认为 B”可用 mix A up with B。

example.english: I mixed up the two meeting times and arrived an hour early.
example.chinese: 我把两个会议时间弄混了，提前一小时到了。

application.prompt: I called my new classmate Tom because I ___ him ___ his brother. A. brought; with B. mixed; up with
application.solution: B。解析：mix sb up with sb 表示“把某人和另一个人弄混”；本句误认了两兄弟。

grammar: 短语 有效利用某物
collocations: put old boxes to good use; put your skills to good use; make good use of time
commonMistake: 固定结构是 put sth to good use；sth 放在 put 与 to good use 之间。

example.english: Our art teacher put the empty bottles to good use by making flower vases.
example.chinese: 美术老师把空瓶子有效利用起来，做成了花瓶。

application.prompt: The club ___ its spare room ___ good use as a reading corner. A. made; for B. put; to
application.solution: B。解析：put sth to good use 是“有效利用某物”；空房间被改作阅读角，符合这一搭配。

collocations: the human brain; brain research; use your brain
commonMistake: brain 可指大脑，也可借指智力；mind 多指思维或心智，不能把两词在所有语境中互换。

example.english: The human brain keeps working even while we sleep.
example.chinese: 即使在睡觉时，人脑也仍在工作。

application.prompt: The doctor used a scan to study the patient's ___. A. mind B. brain
application.solution: B。解析：scan 检查的是身体器官 brain（大脑）；mind 指思维或心智，不是可扫描的器官。

collocations: a bicycle chain; a chain of events; a chain store
commonMistake: chain 作“链条”时可数；a chain of 表示“一连串”，不要漏掉介词 of。

example.english: A broken chain kept the bicycle from moving.
example.chinese: 链条断了，导致这辆自行车无法行驶。

application.prompt: One mistake led to another in a ___ of events. A. row B. chain
application.solution: B。解析：a chain of events 指“接连发生的一连串事件”；row 不表示这种因果连续性。

collocations: a stable job; remain stable; stable conditions
commonMistake: stable 是形容词，名词 stability 表示“稳定性”；不要把 stable 当作副词修饰动词。

example.english: The patient is now in a stable condition.
example.chinese: 病人的病情现在稳定。

application.prompt: The bridge stayed ___ during the strong wind. A. stability B. stable
application.solution: B。解析：stay 后用形容词 stable 作表语；stability 是名词，意为“稳定性”。

collocations: retell a story; retell the event in your own words; retelling task
commonMistake: retell 是及物动词，后直接接故事或经历；不要说 retell about a story。

example.english: At the end of class, Leo retold the story in his own words.
example.chinese: 下课前，利奥用自己的话复述了这个故事。

application.prompt: Please ___ the main events without looking at the book. A. tell about B. retell
application.solution: B。解析：retell the events 表示“复述事件”；retell 后直接接宾语，不需要 about。

collocations: memorize a poem; memorize the spelling; memorize facts
commonMistake: memorize 的名词是 memorization；英式拼法 memorise 也正确，写作中应保持拼写一致。

example.english: Nora memorized the poem before the speaking contest.
example.chinese: 诺拉在演讲比赛前背熟了这首诗。

application.prompt: To remember the new words, I ___ them in short groups. A. memory B. memorize
application.solution: B。解析：句中需要谓语动词 memorize（记住）；memory 是名词，不能直接充当谓语。

collocations: tick the correct box; put a tick next to an answer; tick off a list
commonMistake: 表示“打钩”时 tick 是动词；表示勾号时是名词，前面可用 a。

example.english: Tick the box if you can come to the meeting.
example.chinese: 如果你能来开会，请在方框里打钩。

application.prompt: There was a small ___ beside every correct answer. A. ticked B. tick
application.solution: B。解析：a 后需要名词 tick（勾号）；ticked 是动词过去式或过去分词。

collocations: their grandson; a loving grandfather; grandsons and granddaughters
commonMistake: grandson 指儿子或女儿的儿子；对应女性是 granddaughter，不能用 grandson 泛指孙辈。

example.english: My grandson visits me every Sunday afternoon.
example.chinese: 我的外孙每周日下午都来看我。

application.prompt: Mr Wu has one granddaughter and two ___. A. grandsons B. granddaughters
application.solution: A。解析：题干已给出一名孙女，另外两名男性孙辈是 grandsons。

grammar: 短语 经历；仔细察看
collocations: go through a difficult time; go through the notes; go through customs
commonMistake: go through 可表示“经历”或“逐项检查”；不能把它误写成表示穿过空间的 go across。

example.english: We went through the old letters together and found a family photo.
example.chinese: 我们一起仔细翻看旧信，找到了一张家庭照片。

application.prompt: Before handing in the report, check every page and ___ it carefully. A. go across B. go through
application.solution: B。解析：go through the report 表示“仔细检查报告”；go across 强调从一边走到另一边。

collocations: What happened to your bag?; happen to meet sb; happen to sb
commonMistake: 询问某人或某物遭遇了什么用 What happened to ...?；happen to do sth 表示“碰巧做某事”。

example.english: I happened to meet my primary-school teacher at the station.
example.chinese: 我碰巧在车站遇见了小学老师。

application.prompt: We ___ meet the school band while we were buying tickets. A. happened to B. happened for
application.solution: A。解析：happen to do 表示“碰巧做某事”；句中两人意外遇到校乐队，符合此结构。

collocations: keep the rules in mind; keep in mind that ...; bear sth in mind
commonMistake: keep sth in mind 中 sth 放在 keep 与 in mind 之间；后接完整从句时用 keep in mind that。

example.english: Keep the meeting time in mind so you do not arrive late.
example.chinese: 记住开会时间，这样你就不会迟到。

application.prompt: The sign says the pool closes at six, so please ___ that ___ mind. A. keep; in B. hold; on
application.solution: A。解析：keep that in mind 表示“把这件事记在心里”；本句提醒大家记住泳池关闭时间。

collocations: in this case; a difficult case; a case of mistaken identity
commonMistake: case 作“情况”时常见于 in this case；in case 表示“以防”，两种结构意义不同。

example.english: In this case, taking the earlier train is the safer choice.
example.chinese: 在这种情况下，乘坐较早的一班火车更稳妥。

application.prompt: The road is closed, so ___ we should take the bridge instead. A. in the case B. in this case
application.solution: B。解析：in this case 表示“在这种情况下”；句子根据道路封闭这一事实作出选择。

grammar: 短语 就某人的情况而言
collocations: in my case; in her case; in the case of young children
commonMistake: in sb’s case 中 sb 要换成所有格（my/his/her）；它讨论个人情况，不等于 in case（以防）。

example.english: In my case, a short walk helps me think clearly.
example.chinese: 就我而言，短暂散步有助于理清思路。

application.prompt: Lily learns best by drawing pictures. ___, making a diagram is a good study method. A. In her case B. In case
application.solution: A。解析：In her case 表示“就她的情况而言”；第二句承接 Lily 的个人学习习惯。

collocations: an opera singer; go to the opera; a famous opera
commonMistake: opera 指有音乐和舞台表演的歌剧；它不是普通的 play（话剧）。

example.english: My parents took me to the opera for my birthday.
example.chinese: 父母带我去看歌剧庆祝生日。

application.prompt: The story is told through singing and orchestral music, so it is an ___. A. opera B. exhibition
application.solution: A。解析：歌唱与管弦乐共同讲述舞台故事，符合 opera（歌剧）的特点。

collocations: have a picnic; go on a picnic; a picnic basket
commonMistake: picnic 前常用 have/go on；表示正在野餐可说 have a picnic，动词 picnic 的现在分词要双写 c。

example.english: We had a picnic under the trees beside the lake.
example.chinese: 我们在湖边的树下野餐。

application.prompt: If the weather stays sunny, we can ___ by the river. A. make a picnic B. have a picnic
application.solution: B。解析：英语中固定搭配是 have a picnic（野餐）；make a picnic 不自然。

grammar: v. 原谅；请再说一遍；interj. 抱歉
collocations: Pardon me?; pardon sb for doing sth; beg your pardon
commonMistake: 听不清时可礼貌地说 Pardon?；表示原谅某人用 pardon sb，不能把 pardon 和 excuse 的结构随意互换。

example.english: Pardon me, could you say the station name again?
example.chinese: 不好意思，您能再说一遍车站的名字吗？

application.prompt: “The next stop is Green Park.” “___? I couldn't hear you.” A. Pardon B. Forgive
application.solution: A。解析：单独说 Pardon? 是礼貌地请对方重复；forgive 需要宾语，不能这样使用。

collocations: hear a gunshot; the sound of a gunshot; gunshot wound
commonMistake: gunshot 是可数名词，单数前可用 a；若强调枪声，可说 the sound of a gunshot。

example.english: The hikers heard a gunshot far away in the forest.
example.chinese: 徒步者听见森林深处传来一声枪响。

application.prompt: The police heard one loud ___ shortly after midnight. A. gunshot B. gunsound
application.solution: A。解析：one loud 后接可数名词 gunshot，表示“一声枪响”；gunsound 不是规范词。

grammar: adj. 成年的；n. 成年人
collocations: a grown-up conversation; ask a grown-up for help; grown-up responsibilities
commonMistake: grown-up 作名词时指成年人；不要将它与 grown（grow 的过去分词）当作完全相同的词性。

example.english: The children asked a grown-up to help them cross the busy road.
example.chinese: 孩子们请一位成年人帮他们穿过繁忙的马路。

application.prompt: When the children got lost, they asked a nearby ___ for help. A. grow B. grown-up
application.solution: B。解析：ask a grown-up for help 是“向成年人求助”；grow 是动词，不能指人。

collocations: recall a memory; recall doing sth; recall that ...
commonMistake: recall doing 表示“记得做过某事”；回忆过去经历时不用 recall to do。

example.english: I recall seeing that painting at the museum last year.
example.chinese: 我记得去年在博物馆见过那幅画。

application.prompt: Emma clearly ___ locking the door before she left. A. recalls B. recall
application.solution: A。解析：主语 Emma 是第三人称单数，谓语用 recalls；recall locking 表示“记得锁过门”。

collocations: a grapevine in the garden; grapevine leaves; grow grapevines
commonMistake: grapevine 可指结葡萄的藤；口语里 hear sth through the grapevine 是“听到传闻”，不要按字面理解成电话网络。

example.english: A grapevine covered the sunny wall of my uncle's garden.
example.chinese: 一株葡萄藤爬满了叔叔花园里向阳的墙面。

application.prompt: In autumn, the ___ in our garden is heavy with purple fruit. A. grapevine B. pine tree
application.solution: A。解析：葡萄藤在秋天结紫色果实，句中应填 grapevine；pine tree 是松树。

grammar: v. 促进；使增长；n. 提高；帮助
collocations: boost confidence; boost sales; a boost to the local economy
commonMistake: boost 作动词后直接接被提升的对象；作名词时常用 a boost to sth。

example.english: Daily practice gave her confidence a real boost.
example.chinese: 每天练习大大增强了她的信心。

application.prompt: The new sports program aims to ___ students' confidence. A. boost B. booster
application.solution: A。解析：aims to 后接动词原形 boost，表示“增强信心”；booster 是名词。

collocations: to start with, ...; start with an example; to begin with
commonMistake: to start with 常用于列举理由或说明开端；句首作连接语时后面通常加逗号。

example.english: To start with, we need to decide who will bring the maps.
example.chinese: 首先，我们需要决定由谁带地图。

application.prompt: ___, let's check the weather before planning the hike. A. At first place B. To start with
application.solution: B。解析：To start with 用来引出首先要做的事；句子先检查天气再规划徒步。

collocations: a short-term plan; short-term memory; short-term effects
commonMistake: short-term 作复合形容词时通常加连字符并放在名词前；不要写成 short time plan。

example.english: The school introduced a short-term course in first aid.
example.chinese: 学校开设了一门短期急救课程。

application.prompt: The shelter needs a ___ solution for tonight, then a permanent one. A. short-term B. shortly
application.solution: A。解析：solution 前需要形容词 short-term（短期的）；shortly 是副词，不能修饰名词。

collocations: a long-term goal; long-term benefits; long-term planning
commonMistake: long-term 表示持续较长时间，常作定语；名词形式可用 the long term。

example.english: Learning to read regularly has long-term benefits.
example.chinese: 坚持阅读能带来长期益处。

application.prompt: The team is planning for ___ success, not just one good season. A. longly B. long-term
application.solution: B。解析：success 前需要 long-term 作形容词，表示“长期的”；longly 不是规范副词。

collocations: a useful technique; a technique for memorizing words; breathing technique
commonMistake: technique 指做事的方法或技巧；technical 是形容词“技术的”，不能用来表示某一种技巧。

example.english: The coach taught us a breathing technique for staying calm.
example.chinese: 教练教了我们一种保持冷静的呼吸技巧。

application.prompt: The pianist practised a new ___ to play the fast passage clearly. A. technique B. technical
application.solution: A。解析：a new 后接名词 technique，指演奏技巧；technical 是形容词。

collocations: a passage from a novel; read the passage; a narrow passage
commonMistake: passage 可指文章的一段或狭窄通道；paragraph 专指文章段落，不能表示走廊。

example.english: We read a short passage about life in the Arctic.
example.chinese: 我们读了一段关于北极生活的短文。

application.prompt: The guide led us through a narrow stone ___ between the rooms. A. paragraph B. passage
application.solution: B。解析：rooms 之间的狭窄石头通道是 passage；paragraph 是文章段落。

grammar: adj. 很可能的；adv. 可能
collocations: be likely to do; it is likely that ...; a likely reason
commonMistake: 作形容词时用 be likely to do 或 It is likely that...；likely 作副词时可放在 will 后。

example.english: It is likely to rain before the football match ends.
example.chinese: 足球比赛结束前很可能会下雨。

application.prompt: Dark clouds are gathering, so it will ___ rain soon. A. likely B. likelihood
application.solution: A。解析：will 后可接副词 likely，表示“很可能”；likelihood 是名词，不能放在 will 后作谓语。

collocations: wear out shoes; wear yourself out; be worn out after work
commonMistake: wear out 的过去式是 wore out，过去分词是 worn out；表示“筋疲力尽”时常用 be worn out。

example.english: Walking in the rain wore out the soles of my old shoes.
example.chinese: 在雨中走路把我的旧鞋底磨坏了。

application.prompt: After a twelve-hour shift, the nurses were completely ___. A. wear out B. worn out
application.solution: B。解析：be worn out 表示“筋疲力尽”；句中 were 后需要过去分词形容词 worn out。

collocations: discuss a problem; discuss the plan with sb; discuss how to help
commonMistake: discuss 是及物动词，后直接接话题；不要说 discuss about the problem。

example.english: We discussed how to make the school garden more welcoming.
example.chinese: 我们讨论了怎样让校园花园更宜人。

application.prompt: The class will ___ the best way to reduce food waste. A. discuss B. discuss about
application.solution: A。解析：discuss the best way 是正确结构；discuss 后直接接讨论内容，不加 about。

collocations: a digital image; an image of the city; public image
commonMistake: image 可指照片、脑海中的形象或公众形象；表示具体照片时 picture 更日常，但二者不能在所有搭配中互换。

example.english: The website uses a clear image of the new library.
example.chinese: 这个网站使用了一张新图书馆的清晰图片。

application.prompt: The charity wants to improve its public ___ by sharing its work. A. imagine B. image
application.solution: B。解析：public image 指“公众形象”；imagine 是动词，不能放在形容词 public 后。

collocations: a line graph; a graph of test scores; draw a graph
commonMistake: graph 通常用线或坐标展示数据变化；paragraph 是文字段落，不能用来表示数据图表。

example.english: The graph shows how the river level changed during the storm.
example.chinese: 图表显示了暴风雨期间河流水位的变化。

application.prompt: A ___ makes it easy to compare the monthly temperatures. A. graph B. paragraph
application.solution: A。解析：graph 能用图形呈现并比较温度数据；paragraph 是文字段落。

collocations: organize a meeting; organize information; well-organized notes
commonMistake: organize 的名词为 organization；英式拼法 organise 也正确，派生形容词 organized 常用连字符构成 well-organized。

example.english: Our class organized a book sale to raise money for the library.
example.chinese: 我们班组织了一场图书义卖，为图书馆筹款。

application.prompt: The volunteers will ___ the clean-up day next Saturday. A. organization B. organize
application.solution: B。解析：will 后接动词原形 organize，表示“组织”；organization 是名词。

grammar: n. 景色；观点；v. 观看
collocations: a view of the sea; in my view; view a video
commonMistake: view 作名词可指景色或观点，作动词表示观看；表达个人看法可说 in my view，不说 according to my view。

example.english: From the hill, we enjoyed a wide view of the valley.
example.chinese: 从山上望去，我们欣赏到了山谷的开阔景色。

application.prompt: ___, every student should have a chance to speak. A. In my view B. In my viewing
application.solution: A。解析：In my view 是“在我看来”的固定表达；本句引出说话者对课堂机会的看法。

collocations: an effective method; effective in reducing waste; work effectively
commonMistake: effective 的名词是 effect，副词是 effectively；effective 强调产生预期效果，efficient 强调省时省力。

example.english: Wearing a helmet is an effective way to protect your head.
example.chinese: 戴头盔是保护头部的有效方法。

application.prompt: The school tried a more ___ way to remind students to save water. A. effect B. effective
application.solution: B。解析：way 前需用形容词 effective，表示“有效的”；effect 是名词。

collocations: a car engine; engine noise; start the engine
commonMistake: engine 通常指机器或车辆的发动机；engineer 是工程师，不能因拼写相近而互换。

example.english: The mechanic checked the engine before the long drive.
example.chinese: 长途驾驶前，修理工检查了发动机。

application.prompt: The bus driver turned off the ___ before leaving the vehicle. A. engine B. engineer
application.solution: A。解析：turn off 的宾语是 bus 的 engine（发动机）；engineer 指工程师。

grammar: n. 燃料；v. 给……提供燃料
collocations: save fuel; fuel consumption; fuel a car with petrol
commonMistake: fuel 作名词通常不可数；fuel 作动词时可接交通工具或某种情绪作宾语。

example.english: The research ship carries enough fuel for the journey.
example.chinese: 这艘科考船带了足够的燃料完成这趟航行。

application.prompt: To cut costs, the airline is trying to use less ___. A. fuel B. fuels
application.solution: A。解析：fuel 作“燃料”通常为不可数名词；less 后用 fuel，不加复数 s。

collocations: anxiety about exams; feel anxiety; reduce anxiety
commonMistake: anxiety 是不可数名词，形容词是 anxious；说“对考试感到焦虑”可用 anxiety about exams。

example.english: Talking with her teacher helped ease her anxiety about the test.
example.chinese: 和老师谈过后，她对考试的焦虑减轻了。

application.prompt: Ben felt ___ about speaking in front of the whole school. A. anxiously B. anxiety
application.solution: B。解析：felt 后可接名词 anxiety 表示感到焦虑；anxiously 是副词，需修饰动作。

grammar: n. 地址；v. 写地址；处理
collocations: home address; address an envelope; address a problem
commonMistake: address 作动词时可表示“处理问题”或“向……讲话”；给信封写地址也用 address，不能说 write an address on someone。

example.english: Please write your return address on the back of the envelope.
example.chinese: 请把回邮地址写在信封背面。

application.prompt: Before mailing the letter, remember to ___ the envelope clearly. A. address B. address to
application.solution: A。解析：address the envelope 表示“在信封上写地址”；该用法后面不加 to。

collocations: enter a password; reset your password; a strong password
commonMistake: password 是可数名词；网络操作常用 enter/type a password，密码本身不能“记住账户”。

example.english: I changed my password after receiving the security alert.
example.chinese: 收到安全提醒后，我更改了密码。

application.prompt: The website won't open your account until you enter the correct ___. A. password B. passport
application.solution: A。解析：登录账户需要输入 password（密码）；passport 是旅行证件。

collocations: open a bank account; a user account; an account of the trip
commonMistake: account 作“账户”时常与 open/use 搭配；on account of 表示“因为”，不可误写成 on the account of。

example.english: My brother opened a savings account at the local bank.
example.chinese: 我哥哥在当地银行开了一个储蓄账户。

application.prompt: You need a user ___ to save your settings on this website. A. count B. account
application.solution: B。解析：user account 指网站用户账户；count 是“数数”，不表示登录账户。

collocations: increase by ten percent; increase the price; an increase in visitors
commonMistake: increase by 后接增幅，increase to 后接达到的数值；名词前可用 an。

example.english: The number of visitors increased by twenty percent this year.
example.chinese: 今年的参观人数增加了百分之二十。

application.prompt: The water level rose from 2 metres to 3 metres, an ___ of 1 metre. A. increase B. increasing
application.solution: A。解析：an 后接名词 increase，表示“增长”；句中数量从 2 米升到 3 米。

collocations: blood pressure; blood type; donate blood
commonMistake: blood 作“血液”时通常不可数；表示流血的动作要用动词 bleed，不说 blood from a cut 作动词。

example.english: The nurse took a small sample of blood for the test.
example.chinese: 护士抽取了一小份血样进行检查。

application.prompt: The hospital is asking people to ___ blood this weekend. A. bloody B. donate
application.solution: B。解析：donate blood 表示“献血”；bloody 是形容词，意为“血腥的/满是血的”。

collocations: a deep wound; wound a soldier; treat a wound
commonMistake: wound 表示“伤口/使受伤”时读 /wuːnd/；它也可能是 wind 的过去式，需按上下文判断含义。

example.english: The nurse cleaned the wound on his arm.
example.chinese: 护士清洗了他手臂上的伤口。

application.prompt: The first-aid team covered the ___ with a clean bandage. A. wound B. wounder
application.solution: A。解析：bandage 包扎的是 wound（伤口）；wounder 不是表示伤口的词。

collocations: a shopping mall; go to the mall; a mall entrance
commonMistake: mall 指大型购物商场；shopping centre 是常见同义表达，不要与 market（市场）在所有场景中混用。

example.english: We met at the mall after school to buy a birthday gift.
example.chinese: 放学后我们在购物商场碰面，去买生日礼物。

application.prompt: The new ___ has a cinema, a food court and more than a hundred shops. A. market B. mall
application.solution: B。解析：有电影院、美食广场和许多商店的大型购物场所是 mall（购物商场）。

grammar: n. 笔记本；笔记本电脑
collocations: write in a notebook; a notebook computer; keep a notebook
commonMistake: notebook 可指纸质笔记本，也可指笔记本电脑；paper notebook 表示纸本时可避免歧义。

example.english: I keep a small notebook in my bag for new English words.
example.chinese: 我在包里放了一本小笔记本，记英语新词。

application.prompt: Please write the homework in your ___ so you won't forget it. A. notebook B. notebook computer
application.solution: A。解析：写作业并记下来需要纸质 notebook；notebook computer 是笔记本电脑。

collocations: a red squirrel; a squirrel's tail; squirrels collect nuts
commonMistake: squirrel 的复数是 squirrels；所有格写 squirrel's，不要遗漏复数或所有格标记。

example.english: A squirrel hid an acorn under the garden bench.
example.chinese: 一只松鼠把橡子藏在花园长椅下面。

application.prompt: We watched two ___ carry nuts up the tree. A. squirrel B. squirrels
application.solution: B。解析：two 后接复数 squirrels；本句有两只松鼠。

collocations: a handful of nuts; nut allergy; tighten a nut
commonMistake: nut 可指坚果，也可指螺母；坚果统称时常用复数 nuts，不能与 nutritious（有营养的）混为同一个词。

example.english: The recipe adds chopped nuts for extra crunch.
example.chinese: 这道食谱加入切碎的坚果来增加酥脆口感。

application.prompt: The mechanic tightened the metal ___ that held the wheel in place. A. nut B. nutrition
application.solution: A。解析：固定车轮的金属螺母是 nut；nutrition 意为“营养”。

grammar: adj. 野生的；自然生长的
collocations: wild animals; grow wild; in the wild
commonMistake: wild 修饰动物或植物；表示“在野外”说 in the wild，副词“疯狂地/猛烈地”是 wildly。

example.english: We saw wild elephants from a safe distance.
example.chinese: 我们在安全距离外看到了野生大象。

application.prompt: The researchers observed the birds living freely ___, not in cages. A. wildly B. in the wild
application.solution: B。解析：in the wild 表示“在野外”；此处说明鸟类生活在自然环境中，而非笼中。

collocations: a school of dolphins; dolphin show; protect dolphins
commonMistake: dolphin 的复数是 dolphins；表示一群海豚可用 a pod 或 a school of dolphins。

example.english: A dolphin leaped out of the water beside the boat.
example.chinese: 一只海豚在船边跃出水面。

application.prompt: We saw a group of ___ swimming near the reef. A. dolphins B. dolphin
application.solution: A。解析：a group of 后接可数名词复数 dolphins；这里指一群海豚。

collocations: recognize a face; recognize sb as; recognize the importance of sth
commonMistake: recognize 的名词是 recognition；英式拼法 recognise 也正确，注意它不是 recognize 的过去式。

example.english: I recognized my old neighbour by her cheerful laugh.
example.chinese: 我凭着她爽朗的笑声认出了老邻居。

application.prompt: Although he wore a hat, I could still ___ him from his voice. A. recognition B. recognize
application.solution: B。解析：could 后接动词原形 recognize，表示“辨认出”；recognition 是名词。

grammar: n. 纲要；轮廓；v. 概述
collocations: write an outline; outline the main points; an outline of the plan
commonMistake: outline 作动词时后接要点或计划；作名词时常说 an outline of sth，不要把 outline 和 online 混淆。

example.english: The speaker outlined the three steps of the experiment.
example.chinese: 演讲者概述了实验的三个步骤。

application.prompt: Before writing the essay, Jia made an ___ of her main ideas. A. outline B. online
application.solution: A。解析：an outline of ideas 是“要点提纲”；online 表示“在线”，不合语境。

collocations: divide the class into groups; divide the cake equally; divide by five
commonMistake: divide A into B 表示“把 A 分成 B”；数学除法用 divide A by B，介词不能互换。

example.english: The teacher divided the class into four reading groups.
example.chinese: 老师把全班分成了四个阅读小组。

application.prompt: If you ___ 24 ___ 6, the answer is 4. A. divide; into B. divide; by
application.solution: B。解析：divide 24 by 6 表示“24 除以 6”；divide ... into 用于分组或划分部分。

grammar: 短语 把某物分成（若干部分）
collocations: divide a cake into slices; divide a book into chapters; be divided into teams
commonMistake: 结构为 divide sth into + 类别或部分；被动式是 sth be divided into...。

example.english: The museum is divided into five sections by historical period.
example.chinese: 这座博物馆按历史时期分成五个展区。

application.prompt: The coach ___ the players ___ two teams for the practice match. A. divided; into B. divided; by
application.solution: A。解析：divide the players into two teams 表示“把球员分成两队”；by 不用于划分组别。

collocations: fully understand; fully grown; fully aware of
commonMistake: fully 是副词，修饰动词、形容词或过去分词；对应形容词是 full，不能说 full understand。

example.english: The instructions were fully explained before the activity began.
example.chinese: 活动开始前，说明已被充分讲解。

application.prompt: The child was not ___ ready to cross the busy street alone. A. full B. fully
application.solution: B。解析：ready 前需要副词 fully 修饰，表示“完全准备好”；full 是形容词。

collocations: a one-size-fits-all solution; one-size-fits-all advice; avoid one-size-fits-all rules
commonMistake: one-size-fits-all 是复合形容词，通常用连字符；它指不考虑个人差异、对所有人一概适用的方案。

example.english: A one-size-fits-all schedule may not work for students with different needs.
example.chinese: 一刀切的日程安排可能不适合需求各异的学生。

application.prompt: Because each learner progresses differently, the school rejected a ___ reading plan. A. one-size-fits-all B. one-size-fits
application.solution: A。解析：one-size-fits-all 描述对所有学生相同的通用计划；one-size-fits 不是完整形容词。
